items.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
items.content_html: Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days. Even more surprisingly, supplementing with a simple amino acid called D-serine improved memory and learning, offering a potential new approach to age-related cognitive decline.

items.title: Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, October 12, 2026
items.content_html:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 38221496054.

The short draft and the expand passes

The first script draft came in at 3,003 words against a target of 3,400. The pipeline sent it back for up to two expand passes. The script that shipped is 3,513 words, which is above target, so the expansion overshot. The first draft was short by 397 words and the shipped script is 113 words over the target.

Quality checks on that script: zero AI-tell pattern hits. The Casey-to-Riley voice ratio is 0.82.

Roundup: 44 stories cut, 2 aired out of order

The roundup pool was larger than one segment could air. The airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) dropped 44 stories. That is the design: a cut story stays in the pool and can run on a day that matches it better.

The script stage had a degradation. Two stories still aired after a later block, even after one repair pass on the roundup order. The listener heard two items out of their intended sequence. The pipeline did not fix this and shipped the episode with it.

Citations for the roundup matched 12 of 14. Two roundup citations did not match their sources.

Deep dives: three segments, two citations matched

The episode carried three deep dives: a Business Insider piece on a cookie business that scaled too quickly, an NYT Top Stories piece on a new generation of Inuit creatives in Canada's Arctic, and a Mother Jones piece titled "Stop the Steal Never Stopped." Deep-dive citations matched 2 of 3. One deep-dive citation did not match its source.

The debate question for the episode was: when a talented kid leaves a small town, is that a loss for the town or a success for the kid, and what does the town owe the people who stay?

Audio: three short takes, one retry still short

Text-to-speech returned three segments shorter than their word count predicted. Each got one retry. One of those retries was still short. The pipeline keeps the longer of the two takes for each segment, so the episode drops no content. The one that stayed short is a take that ran short on both attempts, and the longer of those two is what aired.

The rendered episode runs 20.8 minutes at 19.0 MB. The video render is 20.8 minutes at 71.4 MB, and it went to YouTube.

Timing and spend

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific and finished at 1:44 AM Pacific with a success conclusion, 0 minutes late. Fallback 1 started at 2:05 AM Pacific and finished at 2:05 AM Pacific, also a success and 0 minutes late. Fallback 2 started at 3:05 AM Pacific, is the run writing this review, and has no finish time yet.

The script stage ran for 607 seconds and install system dependencies took 710 seconds, the longest step. Deploy to GitHub Pages took 349 seconds. Render episode audio took 300 seconds.

Spend: 59,133 Anthropic input tokens across 19 Claude calls, and 23 Brave Search calls. The feed now holds 257 episodes.

items.title: Integrating Solar Protection as an Envelope Strategy
items.content_html: Heat waves are becoming more and more frequent worldwide, prompting architects to reconsider how building envelopes are conceived and designed. The focus is no longer solely on limiting heat loss during the colder months, but also on controlling how much heat enters buildings during periods of intense solar radiation. By understanding solar shading as a design decision rather than a decorative or interior-conditioning element, it becomes part of passive energy-efficiency strategies that can contribute to thermal and visual comfort while reducing cooling demand.

items.title: What’s open and closed on Columbus Day 2026? Banks, stock markets, Costco, CVS, mail, and more
items.content_html:
Monday holidays, like today’s double feature of Columbus Day and Indigenous Peoples’ Day, can be confusing.

When you layer in the observance’s controversy, it gets even muddier.

Does the federal government recognize Columbus Day, or Indigenous Peoples’ Day, or both?

Read on to find the answers to these questions, some historical facts, and clarification about what exactly remains open and closed today: Monday, October 12, 2026.

A brief history of Columbus Day

Since 1971, Columbus Day has been observed on the second Monday in October. This year, Columbus Day falls on October 12, 2026, which is today.

The day celebrates Christopher Columbus, who is historically credited with “discovering” America, even though indigenous people already inhabited the region.

In 1492, he sailed the ocean blue thanks to funding by King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella of Spain, with the directive to find a route to Asia.

Instead, the expedition aboard the Niña, Pinta, and Santa Maria landed in the Bahamas, then Hispaniola. His mistake helped Spain establish the first American colony in the Caribbean.

Columbus wasn’t exactly the most benevolent leader. As governor of Hispaniola, he enslaved the Taino and Arawak people. As a result, they faced horrific working conditions on mines and plantations.

Columbus forced his Catholic faith on native people using brutal methods. His discovery also kicked off a race of exploration among European nations. These settlers brought new diseases to the Americas, which decimated native populations.

Centuries later, in 1892, President Benjamin Harrison issued a proclamation encouraging Americans to celebrate Columbus Day.

This one-time observance marked the 400th anniversary. President Franklin D. Roosevelt also supported Columbus Day’s observance in 1937, further cementing a 1934 resolution to make it annual. In 1968, the Uniform Monday Holiday Act made it a federal holiday.

Columbus Day has had opponents as early as the 1800s. Anti-immigrant groups did not appreciate how the observance was tied to Catholicism.

More recently, Native American groups have pointed out Columbus’s role in the unethical treatment of their ancestors, and protested his celebration.

Indigenous Peoples’ Day has been presented as a Columbus Day alternative since 1991.

This observance is meant to celebrate the legacy and contributions of Native Americans. Despite President Joe Biden’s proclamation in 2021, it is not a federal holiday, although many states, such as California, formally recognize it.

President Trump walked away from Biden’s dual recognition of both Indigenous Peoples’ Day and Columbus Day and instead solely focused on the latter.

Is mail delivered on Columbus Day?

No. Mail is not delivered on Columbus Day because it is a federal holiday.

Is the Post Office open on Columbus Day?

No. Physical post office locations will be closed. The U.S. Postal Service does not operate on federal holidays.

Are banks open on Columbus Day?

To avoid wasting time, it is best to check in with your banking institution of choice before heading over.

The Federal Reserve will be closed, which typically means most national banks follow suit, but some may choose to remain open.

Chase Bank, for example, says its branches are open on Columbus Day, though Monday is treated as a bank holiday for online transactions. Bank of America, meanwhile, will be closed.

Is the stock market open on Columbus Day?

Yes. Both the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq will be open for buying and selling.

Are schools open on Columbus Day?

Public schools are run by local and state governments, which means they are not required to automatically take federal holidays off.

Private schools have even more freedom in their calendaring. It is best to check in with your students’ institution to know how it handles the holiday.

Are pharmacies open on Columbus Day?

Yes. Just in time for flu season, you are free to stock up on medication on Columbus Day. That includes major chains such as CVS and Walgreens, which should be open normal hours, though it’s always best to check with your local pharmacy.

Are stores and groceries open on Columbus Day?

Yes. Both retail stores and grocery stores would love your business. This includes big box retailers like Walmart and Target, and grocery chains like Kroger and Whole Foods.

Costco warehouses will also be open on the Monday holiday.

Perhaps because of the observance’s controversy, there are not a ton of specific Columbus Day sales, but there are general fall ones to take advantage of.

Are restaurants open on Columbus Day?

Yes. If you don’t feel like cooking or need a sweet treat, restaurants, bakeries, and coffee shops have you covered.
